ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, DE is the median line of $\triangle ABC$, the bisector of $\angle ABC$ intersects DE at point F. If $\angle DFB=32^\circ$ and $\angle A=75^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle AED$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $DE$ is the median line of $\triangle ABC$,\\
thus $DE\parallel BC$,\\
therefore $\angle ADE=\angle ABC$, $\angle DFB=\angle FBC$.\\
Since $\angle DFB=32^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle DFB=\angle FBC=32^\circ$.\\
Since the bisector of $\angle ABC$ intersects $DE$ at point F,\\
thus $\angle DBF=\angle FBC=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=32^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ADE=\angle ABC=2\times 32^\circ=64^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle A=75^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle AED=180^\circ−\angle A−\angle ADE=180^\circ−75^\circ−64^\circ=\boxed{41^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Since $DE$ is the median line of $\triangle ABC$, thus $DE\parallel BC$, therefore $\angle ADE=\angle ABC$ and $\angle DFB=\angle FBC$. Since $\angle DFB=32^\circ$, thus $\angle FBC=32^\circ$. Since the bisector of $\angle ABC$ intersects $DE$ at point F, thus $\angle DBF=\angle FBC=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=32^\circ$, therefore $\angle ADE=\angle ABC=2\times 32^\circ=64^\circ$. Since $\angle A=75^\circ$, thus $\angle AED=180^\circ-\angle A-\angle ADE=180^\circ-75^\circ-64^\circ=\boxed{41^\circ}$.
